_readme: Written by scripts/whats_moving.py after each data refresh. The ten most unusual year-on-year moves across the collection, ranked by how far each is from that series' own history of yearly changes. Sentences are templates filled from the numbers.

items.subject: Energy
items.title: Household electricity bills across Europe
items.question: What does a household actually pay for electricity, taxes included, and where is it dearest?
items.label: Austria
items.unit: EUR per kWh, all taxes included
items.source: Eurostat nrg_pc_204 — electricity prices for household consumers, band DC (2 500–4 999 kWh a year), all taxes and levies included, euro per kWh, semi-annual from 2007
items.note: What a household actually pays, as against the industrial bands in elec-eu and gas-eu. Taxes included on purpose: the tax wedge is most of what separates one country from another. Euro rather than national currency, so the countries are directly comparable and an exchange-rate move shows up in the price.
items.sentence: Household electricity bills across Europe — Austria: up 34.3% on a year earlier in H2 2025, the biggest rise in a record that starts in 2008. The usual yearly change is +2.58%.

items.subject: Money and central banks
items.title: Trade and external accounts
items.question: Which economies run a trade deficit, how big are their reserves, and how much do they owe abroad?
items.label: Egypt · fdi net inflow usd
items.source: World Bank World Development Indicators: trade balance, current account, exports and imports, reserves, external debt, broad money, FDI, remittances and the real effective exchange rate, 30 economies
items.note: Series keys are country|indicator. Annual, and the World Bank lags one to two years; external debt is reported only by low and middle income countries, so it is empty for the advanced economies here. Government debt is not here: the WDI series is central government only and covers a third of these countries in odd years; use imf-weo GGXWDG_NGDP for general government gross debt. Broad money is missing for euro-area members (the ECB reports it for the area) and the REER for Türkiye
items.sentence: Trade and external accounts — Egypt · fdi net inflow usd: down 31.1bn on a year earlier, at 15.5bn in 2025, the sharpest fall in a record that starts in 1971. The usual yearly change is +862.5m.

items.subject: Energy
items.title: Where electricity comes from
items.question: How much power does each country make from coal, gas, nuclear, hydro, wind and solar?
items.label: United Kingdom · Coal
items.source: Ember Yearly Electricity Data and the Energy Institute Statistical Review, via Our World in Data: electricity generated by source, TWh, annual
items.note: Series keys are country|source. Generation, not capacity and not consumption: a country that imports power shows less here than it uses. Coal, gas and oil start in 1985 for most countries; the renewables and nuclear columns reach back to 1965. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure
items.sentence: Where electricity comes from — United Kingdom · Coal: down 82.6% on a year earlier in 2025, the sharpest fall in a record that starts in 1921. The usual yearly change is +0.95%.

items.subject: Prices and the cost of living
items.title: US factory-gate prices by sector
items.question: What American factories charge, industry by industry.
items.label: computer electronic
items.unit: index, as published by BLS; base year varies by series
items.source: BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly
items.note: Base periods differ by series (index = 100 at the series start). Ratios and growth rates only
items.sentence: US factory-gate prices by sector — computer electronic: up 12.3% on a year earlier in Jul 2026. The usual yearly change is +0.57%.

items.subject: Prices and the cost of living
items.title: Pets and vets in the shopping basket
items.question: How much of household spending goes on pets and veterinary services?
items.label: Belgium · CP0935
items.unit: per mille of the consumption basket
items.source: Eurostat HICP item weights — share of veterinary and pet services in each country's consumption basket
items.note: HICP item weights, per-mille of total basket: CP0934 pets and related products, CP0935 veterinary and other services for pets. Dataset serves no 2026 (checked in discover — ECOICOP2 rebase); weights for 2026+ need the successor dataset once Eurostat publishes it. A stored 0 means the country did not collect that item's weight in that year (Kosovo throughout, Iceland to 2021), not a zero share
items.sentence: Pets and vets in the shopping basket — Belgium · CP0935: up 41.8% on a year earlier in 2025, the biggest rise in a record that starts in 2006. The usual yearly change is +1.8%.

items.subject: Transport
items.title: New cars by fuel in Europe
items.question: How fast are electric cars taking over from petrol and diesel, country by country?
items.label: Estonia · Diesel
items.source: Eurostat road_eqr_carpda: new passenger car registrations by motor energy, annual
items.note: Series keys are country|fuel: TOTAL all fuels, PET petrol, DIE diesel, ELC battery electric, ELC_PET_HYB petrol hybrid, ELC_PET_PI plug-in petrol hybrid. Divide ELC by TOTAL for the electric share. The hybrid split exists only from 2017 and some countries report it late; the UK stops after 2019
items.sentence: New cars by fuel in Europe — Estonia · Diesel: down 70.4% on a year earlier in 2025, the sharpest fall in a record that starts in 2014. The usual yearly change is -0.87%.

items.subject: Mining, oil and gas
items.title: Mining output in Europe
items.question: Is mining and quarrying, and metal-making, producing more or less, country by country?
items.label: Bulgaria · Mining and quarrying
items.source: Eurostat sts_inpr_m: production in industry, seasonally and calendar adjusted, 2021 = 100, monthly: mining and quarrying (B), oil and gas extraction (B06), metal ores (B07), other mining and quarrying (B08), basic metals (C24)
items.note: Series keys are country|activity. Volume indices, 2021 = 100. The oil-and-gas and metal-ore lines exist only for countries that have them (Norway, Sweden, Poland, Türkiye); empty combinations are dropped
items.sentence: Mining output in Europe — Bulgaria · Mining and quarrying: down 48.3% on a year earlier in Jun 2026, the sharpest fall in a record that starts in 2001. The usual yearly change is -0.38%.

items.subject: Energy
items.title: EU renewable energy targets
items.question: How far is each EU country along the official renewables share, in power, heat and transport?
items.label: Greece · Electricity
items.source: Eurostat nrg_ind_ren: share of energy from renewable sources, the official figure behind the EU targets, annual since 2004
items.note: Series keys are country|measure: REN overall (gross final energy consumption), REN_ELC electricity, REN_TRA transport, REN_HEAT_CL heating and cooling. The Renewable Energy Directive's accounting rules, so the electricity share differs from Ember's generation share in renewables-share. Türkiye is not in this table
items.sentence: EU renewable energy targets — Greece · Electricity: up 9.65 points on a year earlier, at 60.9% in 2025, the biggest rise in a record that starts in 2005. The usual yearly change is +2.17 points.
